statement: A current record lists the external and internal issues the organisation has judged relevant to its purpose and to the intended outcomes of its ISMS.
evidence_hint: context/issues register (e.g. PESTLE/SWOT or ISMS context document); isms_scope

statement: The context record states whether climate change was judged a relevant issue for the ISMS, and gives the conclusion either way.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.4.1 as amended by Amd 1:2024 (amendment text not verified; the supplied standard copy is unamended)
in_force_note: Added by ISO/IEC 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024 (published Feb 2024); in scope for certification audits against the amended standard. Not verified against the amendment text (the supplied copy of the standard is unamended).

statement: The issues record has been revisited since the last management review, or its review date falls within the organisation's defined review cycle.
evidence_hint: context/issues register (version history); isms_audit_reports (management review minutes)

statement: A record names the interested parties relevant to the ISMS (e.g. customers, regulators, staff, suppliers, shareholders).
For each listed interested party, the record states its requirements that are relevant to information security, including legal, regulatory and contractual ones.
The record states which of the identified requirements the organisation has decided to address through the ISMS.
in_force_note: New in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The transition from the 2013 edition ended 31 Oct 2025, so it now applies to every certified ISMS.

statement: The requirements analysis shows that climate-related requirements of interested parties were considered, whether or not any were found.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.4.2 note added by Amd 1:2024 (amendment text not verified). A note, not a 'shall': the organisation is not obliged to record climate requirements
in_force_note: Added by ISO/IEC 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024 (published Feb 2024); in scope for certification audits against the amended standard. Not verified against the amendment text (the supplied copy of the standard is unamended).

statement: A documented ISMS scope statement exists and names the organisational units, locations, services and assets covered.
The scope statement identifies the interfaces and dependencies between activities inside the ISMS and those performed by other organisations or outside the scope.
Any exclusion from the scope is justified by reference to the context issues (4.1) and interested-party requirements (4.2).
The scope statement matches the scope stated on the certificate or audit reports and reflects the organisation's current services and sites.
The ISMS documentation identifies the processes that make up the ISMS (e.g. risk assessment, internal audit, incident management) and how they interact.
evidence_hint: ISMS manual or process map; security_policy

statement: Records show each identified ISMS process has been operated in the last 12 months (e.g. a risk assessment run, an audit performed, a management review held).
The information security policy and objectives are approved by top management and are consistent with the organisation's stated strategic direction.
Top management has allocated resources to the ISMS, shown by an approved budget, headcount or tooling decision in the last 12 months.
Top management attended or chaired the most recent management review and recorded decisions on the ISMS.
Top management has communicated the importance of information security to staff in the last 12 months (e.g. all-hands message, policy launch note).
The top-level information security policy includes, or points to, a framework for setting information security objectives.
The policy contains an explicit commitment to satisfy applicable information security requirements.
The policy contains an explicit commitment to continual improvement of the ISMS.
The policy is available as a controlled document, has been communicated to staff, and is available to interested parties as the organisation decided.
evidence_hint: security_policy (intranet page, distribution record, public copy if any)

statement: A document assigns responsibility and authority for ensuring the ISMS conforms to ISO/IEC 27001.
A document assigns responsibility and authority for reporting ISMS performance to top management.
The assigned security roles have been communicated within the organisation (e.g. org chart or RACI published on the intranet), and the named holders are current staff.
A record identifies the risks and opportunities to the ISMS itself (not only information security risks), drawing on the context issues and interested-party requirements.
Each identified ISMS risk or opportunity has a planned action and a stated way to evaluate whether the action worked.
The planned actions have owners and status updates, and at least one has been evaluated for effectiveness.
The risk methodology defines risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing risk assessments.
The methodology identifies risks as loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability of information within the ISMS scope.
The methodology defines how consequences and likelihood are rated and how they combine into a risk level.
Every entry in the risk register has a named risk owner.
Each risk in the register has been compared with the acceptance criteria and given a treatment priority.

requirement_title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
statement: For each risk requiring treatment, the register or plan records the chosen treatment option (e.g. modify, avoid, share, retain) and the controls selected.

requirement_title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
statement: A Statement of Applicability lists the necessary controls and, for each Annex A control, whether it is included, why, whether it is implemented, and the reason for any exclusion.

requirement_title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
statement: The selected controls were compared against Annex A to confirm no necessary control was omitted (e.g. a mapping or column in the SoA).

requirement_title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
statement: Risk owners have approved the risk treatment plan and formally accepted the residual risks, with dated approvals.

requirement_title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
statement: The SoA's implementation status for a sample of controls matches what the assessment observes (a control marked implemented is in fact operating).
evidence_hint: statement_of_applicability; control evidence for sampled controls

statement: Documented information security objectives exist, are consistent with the policy, and are measurable where practicable.
For each objective the plan states what will be done, resources needed, who is responsible, the deadline and how results will be evaluated.
Progress on each objective has been monitored, with recorded measurements or status against target in the last 12 months.
in_force_note: New in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The transition from the 2013 edition ended 31 Oct 2025, so it now applies to every certified ISMS.

statement: A procedure or rule states how changes to the ISMS (scope, processes, roles, policies) are planned and approved before they take effect.
in_force_note: New in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The transition from the 2013 edition ended 31 Oct 2025, so it now applies to every certified ISMS.

statement: The most recent significant ISMS change (e.g. scope change, reorganisation, new site) has a record showing it was planned and approved beforehand.
evidence_hint: ISMS change record; isms_audit_reports (management review minutes)
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.6.3. What counts as a 'change to the ISMS' is not defined; the sample is the assessor's judgment
in_force_note: New in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The transition from the 2013 edition ended 31 Oct 2025, so it now applies to every certified ISMS.

statement: The organisation has recorded the resources the ISMS needs (people, budget, tools) in a plan, budget or management review output.
evidence_hint: isms_audit_reports (management review minutes); ISMS budget or resource plan

statement: The resources recorded as needed were provided: named people are in post and budgeted items were funded or procured.
Competence requirements (skills, qualifications or experience) are defined for roles that affect information security performance.
For a sample of security-relevant role holders, records show they meet the defined competence requirements (certificates, training, CV).
Where a competence gap was identified, a recorded action (training, mentoring, hiring) was taken and its effectiveness evaluated.
Awareness content tells staff about the security policy, their contribution to the ISMS and the consequences of not conforming.
Records show people working under the organisation's control, including contractors in scope, completed awareness activity in the last 12 months.
A communication plan or matrix states, for ISMS-relevant communications, what is communicated, when, to whom and how.
A sample of planned communications (e.g. to staff, customers or regulators) shows they took place as planned.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.7.4. The clause requires the organisation to determine its communication needs; checking that planned communications happened goes one step further

statement: A document-control procedure covers identification, format, review and approval of ISMS documents.
The procedure covers distribution, access, storage, version control, retention and disposal of ISMS documents and records, including documents of external origin.
A sample of ISMS documents each shows an owner, version, approval and review date, and the version in use is the latest approved one.

The documented information the standard requires is present, including scope, policy, risk assessment and treatment process, SoA, objectives, competence evidence, monitoring results, audit programme and results, management review results and nonconformity records.
Criteria (e.g. procedures, standards, thresholds) are defined for the processes that implement risk treatment and the objectives.
Externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the ISMS are identified and a control over each is defined.
For a sample of planned operational changes, records show they were controlled, and any unintended change was reviewed with action taken on adverse effects.
The risk methodology or ISMS calendar sets the interval for repeating the risk assessment and names significant change as a trigger.
A risk assessment was completed within the defined interval, with dated results retained.
For the most recent significant change (e.g. new system, supplier, site), a risk assessment was performed and recorded.
The risk treatment plan assigns each treatment action an owner and a target date.
Records show the treatment actions due in the period were completed, or overdue ones re-approved, and the results retained.
A measurement plan defines what is monitored and measured (processes and controls), the methods, the frequency, and who monitors and who analyses.
Monitoring and measurement results for the last period are recorded.
The results were analysed and used to evaluate ISMS performance and effectiveness, e.g. in a report to management review.
An internal audit programme sets frequency, methods, responsibilities and reporting, and covers the whole ISMS scope, including clauses 4-10 and the applicable Annex A controls, over the audit cycle.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.9.2.1(a)-(b), cl.9.2.2. Full coverage within one cycle is the usual certification-body expectation, not express text

statement: Each audit has defined criteria and scope.
Audits were performed as programmed in the last 12 months by auditors who did not audit their own work.
Audit results were reported to relevant management and retained.
Management review is scheduled at planned intervals (e.g. at least annually) in the ISMS calendar or policy.

A management review was held within the planned interval and its record shows it considered each required input: previous actions, changes in context and in interested-party needs, performance feedback, stakeholder feedback, risk results and improvement opportunities.
The management review record contains decisions on improvement opportunities and on any needed changes to the ISMS.
The ISMS has a defined means of identifying and acting on improvement opportunities (e.g. an improvement log fed by audits, incidents and reviews).
At least one improvement to the ISMS's suitability, adequacy or effectiveness was implemented in the last 12 months and recorded.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.10.1. The clause sets no minimum rate; one recorded improvement per year is the assessor's threshold

statement: A procedure requires nonconformities to be corrected, their causes determined, and similar nonconformities looked for.
Each nonconformity raised in the period is logged with its nature, the action taken and the result.
For a sample of closed nonconformities, the record shows a root-cause analysis and a review of the corrective action's effectiveness.
A top-level information security policy and topic-specific policies (e.g. access control, backup, cryptography) exist and each shows management approval.
The policies have been published to staff and relevant external parties, and records show staff acknowledged them.
Each policy has been reviewed within its defined review interval, or after a significant change, with the review recorded.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.1 [repo description omits the planned-interval review element of the control]

statement: A document defines the information security responsibilities of each security role (e.g. CISO, asset owners, risk owners, incident manager).
Each defined security role is assigned to a named, current person.
The organisation has identified which duties conflict (e.g. requesting vs approving access, developing vs deploying to production) and states they must be held by different people.
For a sample of the conflicting duty pairs, system roles or approval records show different individuals performed each side.
Where segregation is not feasible (e.g. small team), a compensating control such as monitoring or supervisory review is documented.
Management expectations that staff follow security policies are stated in a document staff receive (e.g. code of conduct, onboarding pack, manager guide).
Managers have briefed or required their teams to comply, shown by records such as policy acknowledgement tracking or manager-led briefings in the period.
A current contact list names the authorities to contact (e.g. data protection regulator, CERT-In or national CERT, law enforcement, sector regulator) and when.
The incident procedure states who is authorised to contact authorities and within what timelines for reportable events.
The authority contact list has been verified or updated within the last 12 months.
The organisation records which security forums, industry groups, ISACs or professional bodies it participates in or subscribes to.
There is evidence of active participation in the period (e.g. advisories received and circulated, event attendance).
A documented process names the threat information sources used and how the information is analysed for relevance to the organisation.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: Threat intelligence outputs (e.g. bulletins, assessments) were produced in the period.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: At least one threat intelligence output led to a recorded action (e.g. a risk register update, blocking rule, patch prioritisation).
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: The project management method requires security requirements and risks to be addressed at defined project stages, regardless of project type.
For a sample of projects in the period, project records show a security risk assessment or security requirements sign-off.

requirement_title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
statement: An inventory of information and associated assets (hardware, software, cloud services, data stores) exists for the ISMS scope.

requirement_title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
statement: Every inventory entry has an assigned owner.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.9 [repo description omits the ownership element of the control]

requirement_title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
statement: The inventory has been updated within its defined review cycle, and a sample of live assets (e.g. from cloud console or MDM) is present in it.
evidence_hint: asset_inventory; cloud console or MDM export

requirement_title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
statement: An acceptable use policy states permitted and prohibited uses of information and assets.

requirement_title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
statement: Handling procedures state how information is to be handled at each classification level (storage, sharing, transport, disposal).

requirement_title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
statement: Users have acknowledged the acceptable use rules (e.g. at onboarding or annually).
The leaver and role-change procedure requires return of all organisational assets (devices, badges, tokens, documents).
For a sample of leavers in the period, records show asset return checked against the asset inventory.

A classification scheme defines levels (e.g. public, internal, confidential, restricted) and the criteria for assigning them, taking account of the need to protect secrecy, accuracy and uptime, and of stakeholder requirements.
Information assets in the inventory have a classification assigned.
A labelling procedure states how each classification level is marked on documents, systems and media, consistent with the classification scheme.
A sample of documents or records shows labels matching the procedure (e.g. headers, metadata tags, DLP labels).
evidence_hint: sample labelled documents; tool configuration (e.g. sensitivity labels)

statement: Rules or procedures cover each transfer channel used (e.g. email, file sharing, removable media, courier, verbal), stating the protection required by classification.
Transfers of information with external parties are covered by agreements that include security terms (e.g. NDAs, data-sharing agreements).
Technical settings for the main transfer channels enforce the rules (e.g. email TLS, external sharing restrictions on file-sharing tools).
A topic-specific access control policy defines rules for logical and physical access, based on business and security requirements (e.g. need-to-know, least privilege).
For a sample of systems, actual access configurations follow the policy rules (e.g. role-based groups, no shared admin accounts).
A procedure covers creation, change and removal of identities, requires each identity to be linked to one person (or an owned non-person account), and controls shared identities.
A reconciliation of active accounts in the identity provider against the HR roster shows no active identities for departed staff.
evidence_hint: identity provider export; HR leaver list

statement: Service and other non-person accounts in scope each have a recorded owner.
A procedure governs issuing, resetting and revoking authentication information (passwords, tokens, keys), including identity verification before resets.
Users are given written guidance on keeping authentication information confidential (e.g. no sharing, use of a password manager, reporting compromise).
Default vendor credentials are changed on installation, as shown by configuration baselines or build checklists.
The access policy requires access to be requested and approved before provisioning, and defines the frequency of access reviews.
For a sample of new or changed access in the period, an approval record exists before the access was granted.
Access reviews were completed at the defined frequency for in-scope systems, with inappropriate access removed.
For a sample of leavers, access was removed within the timeframe set by policy.
evidence_hint: access_control_policy; HR leaver list; identity provider logs

statement: A supplier security policy or procedure defines how suppliers are identified, risk-rated and selected based on security risk.
A supplier register lists suppliers with access to the organisation's information or systems, with a risk rating for each.
For a sample of suppliers onboarded in the period, a security due-diligence assessment was completed before contract signature or access.

requirement_title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
statement: A standard set of supplier security clauses exists, varied by supplier type or risk tier.

requirement_title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
statement: A sample of contracts with high-risk suppliers contains agreed security terms (e.g. confidentiality, incident notification, audit rights, return or deletion at exit).

requirement_title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
statement: The supplier process includes requirements for ICT suppliers to pass security requirements to their own sub-suppliers and to disclose critical components or subcontractors.

requirement_title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
statement: For a sample of key ICT suppliers, records show the supply chain was assessed (e.g. sub-processor lists reviewed, SBOM or component provenance obtained).
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.21. What evidence of supply-chain assessment is sufficient is not fixed; the control statement is process-level

requirement_title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
statement: The supplier procedure sets how often each risk tier of supplier is reviewed and what the review covers.

requirement_title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
statement: Reviews of high-risk suppliers were performed at the set frequency (e.g. assurance reports checked, SLA and incident performance reviewed).

requirement_title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
statement: Material changes to supplier services in the period (new features, sub-processors, locations) were assessed for security impact.

requirement_title: Information security for use of cloud services
statement: A cloud services policy or procedure covers selecting, using, managing and exiting cloud services, including security requirements and the shared-responsibility split.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

requirement_title: Information security for use of cloud services
statement: A register of cloud services in use exists, and each has provider assurance evidence (e.g. SOC 2 report, ISO certificate) reviewed in the period.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

requirement_title: Information security for use of cloud services
statement: An exit plan exists for critical cloud services, covering data return and deletion.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

requirement_title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
statement: A documented incident management procedure covers detection, reporting, triage, response, communication and closure.

requirement_title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
statement: Incident management roles (e.g. incident manager, response team, communications lead) are defined with named people and contact details.

requirement_title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
statement: The incident procedure and roles were communicated to those involved, and the plan was exercised (e.g. tabletop) in the last 12 months.

requirement_title: Assessment and decision on information security events
statement: Written criteria define when a security event is classified as an incident, with severity or priority levels.

requirement_title: Assessment and decision on information security events
statement: For a sample of logged events, the record shows an assessment and a decision on whether each was an incident.
Response procedures cover containment, eradication, recovery, escalation and notification to internal and external parties.
For a sample of incidents in the period, the incident record shows the documented steps were followed and the incident was closed.
Where an incident triggered a legal or contractual notification duty, the record shows notification was made within the required time.
The incident procedure requires a post-incident review for significant incidents.
For significant incidents in the period, a post-incident review was recorded and at least one resulting control improvement was tracked to completion.
evidence_hint: incident_log (post-incident reviews); change_management or risk_assessment updates

statement: A procedure covers identifying, collecting, acquiring and preserving evidence of security events, including chain of custody.
Where evidence was collected in the period, a chain-of-custody or evidence-handling record exists.
Business continuity or crisis plans state how security controls are maintained, or which compensating controls apply, during disruption.
The last continuity test or real disruption record shows security requirements (e.g. access control, logging) were considered and kept in place.
Recovery time and recovery point objectives are defined for critical ICT services, derived from a business impact analysis.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: ICT recovery or disaster recovery plans exist for the critical services.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: The ICT recovery plans were tested in the last 12 months and test results compared against the recovery objectives, with gaps actioned.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

requirement_title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
statement: A compliance register lists every law, regulation and contract term that bears on the organisation's information security (e.g. data protection, sector rules, crypto export, customer contracts).

requirement_title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
statement: For each listed requirement the register records how the organisation meets it (e.g. owner, control reference).

requirement_title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
statement: The register has been reviewed and updated within the last 12 months or after a relevant legal change.
A procedure addresses protection of intellectual property, including acquiring software only from legitimate sources and complying with licence terms.
A software licence reconciliation in the period shows installed or subscribed software is within licensed entitlements.
A records retention schedule defines record types, retention periods and storage requirements, reflecting legal and contractual needs.
For a sample of record types, storage settings protect them against deletion and tampering (e.g. access restrictions, immutability, backups) for the retention period.
evidence_hint: records retention schedule; backup; system configuration

requirement_title: Privacy and protection of personal information
statement: A privacy or PII protection policy identifies the privacy laws and contractual terms that apply to the organisation's processing of personal data.

requirement_title: Privacy and protection of personal information
statement: A person or role is responsible for privacy and PII protection (e.g. DPO or privacy lead).

requirement_title: Privacy and protection of personal information
statement: A current record of personal data processing (e.g. data inventory or processing register) exists for the ISMS scope.
A plan sets when the approach to information security will be reviewed independently and what triggers an unscheduled review.
An independent review (internal audit by someone outside the area, or external audit) was performed within the planned interval and its results were reported to management.

requirement_title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards
statement: Managers or control owners are assigned to check compliance with the security policies and standards in their area, at a defined frequency.

requirement_title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards
statement: Compliance reviews (e.g. control self-assessments, technical compliance scans) were performed in the period and non-compliances recorded with actions.
evidence_hint: isms_audit_reports (compliance review records); corrective action log

statement: Operating procedures are documented for key IT activities (e.g. backups, system start-up and shutdown, user administration, monitoring).
The documented procedures are accessible to the personnel who need them (e.g. in a shared runbook or wiki) and are the current approved versions.
A screening procedure defines the background checks required before a person joins (e.g. identity, references, qualifications, criminal record where lawful).
For a sample of joiners in the period, records show the required checks were completed before the start date or before access was granted.
The procedure states when re-screening is performed (e.g. on promotion to a sensitive role or at a set interval).
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.1 (ongoing checks). The trigger and interval are not fixed by the control

statement: The screening procedure scales the depth of checks to the role, the classification of information to be accessed and the perceived risk, and takes applicable law into account.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.1 [repo description omits the legal and proportionality qualifiers of the control]

statement: Employment and contractor agreement templates include information security responsibilities of the individual and the organisation.
A sample of signed agreements for current staff and contractors contains the security terms.

requirement_title: Information security awareness, education and training
statement: An awareness and training programme defines content, audiences (including role-specific training for technical and privileged roles) and frequency.

requirement_title: Information security awareness, education and training
statement: Completion records show in-scope personnel completed the required awareness training within the defined period, with non-completers followed up.

requirement_title: Information security awareness, education and training
statement: Personnel received updates when relevant policies or procedures changed in the period.
A documented disciplinary process covers information security policy violations.
The disciplinary process has been communicated to personnel (e.g. in the handbook, policy acknowledgement or training).

requirement_title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
statement: Contracts or leaver documents define security responsibilities that continue after termination or role change (e.g. confidentiality, return of information).

requirement_title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
statement: For a sample of leavers, records show continuing obligations were communicated at exit (e.g. exit letter or signed acknowledgement).
Confidentiality or NDA templates exist for staff and for external parties, reflecting the organisation's protection needs.
Signed NDAs exist for a sample of staff, contractors and external parties with access to confidential information.
The NDA templates have been reviewed within the organisation's defined review interval.
A remote working policy sets security requirements for work outside the premises (e.g. approved devices, secure connection, physical privacy, handling of printed material).
Technical enforcement for remote access is in place (e.g. VPN or zero-trust gateway with MFA, device compliance checks).
A reporting channel for security events (e.g. email alias, portal, hotline) is defined and published to personnel.
The incident log contains events reported by personnel through the channel in the period, with timestamps showing timely reporting.
Awareness material tells personnel what to report and how.
Physical security perimeters are defined for each in-scope site (e.g. building, floor, server room), with the protection required for each.
A site walkthrough or photo evidence confirms the defined perimeters exist as described (e.g. doors lock, no unprotected openings).
Where the organisation has no own premises in scope (fully remote or cloud-hosted), the SoA records this and relies on provider assurance for hosting facilities.
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 cl.6.1.3(d), A.7.1. How far provider reports can stand in for own perimeter controls is a judgment

statement: Entry controls (e.g. badge readers, locks, reception) are defined for secure areas, with authorisation rules for who may enter.
Visitor logs or access-control system records exist for the period, and visitors are recorded and escorted where required.
Physical access rights to secure areas were reviewed in the period and leavers' badges deactivated.
Physical security measures for offices, rooms and facilities are specified (e.g. locks, restricted signage, no public indication of sensitive rooms).
Inspection shows the specified measures are in place for sampled rooms holding sensitive information or equipment.
Monitoring arrangements for unauthorised physical access are defined for premises (e.g. CCTV, intruder alarms, guards) with responsibility for responding.
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

statement: Monitoring systems were operational throughout the period (e.g. CCTV retention available, alarm test records, guard logs).
source_basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.7.4 ('continuously'). Whether small offices without CCTV can meet 'continuous' monitoring is a judgment
in_force_note: New Annex A control in the 2022 edition (no 2013 equivalent). The 2013 transition ended 31 Oct 2025.

requirement_title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
statement: A documented assessment of physical and environmental threats (e.g. fire, flood, power surge, civil unrest) exists for each in-scope site.

requirement_title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
statement: Protective measures identified by that assessment (e.g. fire suppression, water detection) are installed and have current maintenance or test records.
Rules for working in secure areas are documented (e.g. no unsupervised third parties, no recording devices, areas locked when vacant).
Personnel authorised for secure areas have been made aware of the rules (e.g. briefing record or signed acknowledgement).
A clear desk and clear screen policy defines the rules for papers, removable media and unattended screens.
Automatic screen lock after inactivity is enforced by configuration on endpoints.
Clear desk compliance was checked in the period (e.g. spot-check records) with findings followed up.
Siting requirements for equipment are defined (e.g. servers in locked racks or rooms, screens not overlooked, protection from environmental hazards).
Inspection of sampled equipment locations confirms the siting requirements are met.
Rules for protecting assets off-premises are documented (e.g. not left unattended, carried as hand luggage, authorisation to remove).
Portable devices used off-site have full-disk encryption and remote wipe enabled, per MDM or endpoint reports.
A media handling procedure covers acquisition, use, transport, storage and disposal of removable and other storage media according to classification.
Technical controls restrict or encrypt removable media on endpoints in line with the procedure.
Media disposals in the period are recorded (e.g. destruction certificates or disposal log).
Supporting utilities for critical facilities (power, cooling, telecoms) have protection defined (e.g. UPS, generator, redundant feeds).
UPS, generator or equivalent equipment has current maintenance and test records.
Cabling protection requirements are defined (e.g. cabling in conduits or locked cabinets, separation of power and data, patch panels in secured rooms).
Inspection of sampled cabling and comms rooms confirms the requirements are met.
Maintenance requirements and schedules are defined for in-scope equipment, following supplier recommendations.
Maintenance records show scheduled maintenance was performed by authorised personnel, and equipment sent off-site for repair was cleared of sensitive data or protected.

requirement_title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
statement: A procedure requires equipment containing storage media to be checked, and data and licensed software removed or securely overwritten, before disposal or reuse.

requirement_title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
statement: For a sample of disposed or reissued devices, records show verified wiping or destruction (e.g. wipe report, destruction certificate).
An endpoint device policy sets security requirements for user devices (e.g. registration, encryption, screen lock, patching, anti-malware, remote wipe), including personally owned devices if allowed.
Device management or endpoint reports show in-scope devices meet the required settings (e.g. disk encryption on, OS within support).
The access policy requires privileged access to be authorised separately, limited to those who need it, and held in accounts separate from everyday user accounts.
